title: Faithful relative sheaves over a stack have effective descent
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $q:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ be a morphism of categories fibred in groupoids on $S$-schemes, with morphisms, pullbacks and etale stack descent as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Suppose that $\mathcal G$ is an etale stack and each functor $q_T:\mathcal F(T)\to\mathcal G(T)$ is faithful (injective on each set of arrows). For every $S$-scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal G(T)$ define a presheaf $P_y$ on schemes over $T$ by $P_y(V\xrightarrow{h}T)=\{(x,\phi):x\in\mathcal F(V),\ \phi:h^*y\xrightarrow{\sim}q(x)\}/\cong$, where an isomorphism from $(x,\phi)$ to $(x',\phi')$ is an arrow $a:x\to x'$ with $q(a)\phi=\phi'$, and restrictions use pullback. Assume that each $P_y$ is a sheaf for jointly surjective etale scheme coverings: compatible local classes glue uniquely. Then $\mathcal F$ is an etale stack, meaning that isomorphisms form etale sheaves and every etale descent datum for objects is effective. No representability or atlas hypothesis on either fibred groupoid is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0CKJ (lemma-relative-sheaf-over-stack-is-stack), specialized to the big etale site of S-schemes; inverting the isomorphism in the displayed relative presheaf gives the orientation used here.

proof.text: Fix an etale cover $(T_i\to T)$ and $x,x'\in\mathcal F(T)$. Use the pullbacks and stack convention of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; all overlap arrows below include the canonical pullback identifications. If $a,b:x\to x'$ have equal restrictions, then $q(a),q(b)$ have equal restrictions. The isomorphism-sheaf condition for the assumed stack $\mathcal G$ gives $q(a)=q(b)$, and faithfulness of $q_T$ gives $a=b$. This proves separatedness for the presheaf of isomorphisms of $x,x'$. The same argument applies over every scheme over $T$.

Let $a_i:x|_{T_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}x'|_{T_i}$ agree on $T_i\times_TT_j$. The isomorphism-sheaf condition for $\mathcal G$ in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] glues their images to $b:q(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}q(x')$ over $T$. In the relative presheaf $P_{q(x')}$ compare the classes of $(x,b^{-1})$ and $(x',\mathrm{id})$. They restrict to the same class on each $T_i$, since $q(a_i)b^{-1}|_{T_i}=\mathrm{id}$. Separatedness of this sheaf, which is a hypothesis of the item, makes the global classes equal. Equality of isomorphism classes in a groupoid means there is an isomorphism of representatives (composable isomorphisms and their inverses collapse any zigzag to one arrow). Thus there is $a:x\xrightarrow{\sim}x'$ with $q(a)b^{-1}=\mathrm{id}$, or $q(a)=b$. Faithfulness of $q_{T_i}$ gives $a|_{T_i}=a_i$. Uniqueness follows from step 1. As $T,x,x'$ were arbitrary, isomorphisms in $\mathcal F$ form etale sheaves.

Take an object descent datum: $x_i\in\mathcal F(T_i)$ and $d_{ij}:x_j|_{T_{ij}}\xrightarrow{\sim}x_i|_{T_{ij}}$ with $d_{ij}d_{jk}=d_{ik}$ on triple overlaps, where $T_{ij}=T_i\times_TT_j$. Applying $q$ preserves this equation. Effective descent in the assumed stack $\mathcal G$, with the convention of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids], therefore gives $y\in\mathcal G(T)$ and isomorphisms $e_i:y|_{T_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}q(x_i)$ such that $q(d_{ij})e_j=e_i$. In the presheaf $P_y$, the classes of $(x_i,e_i)$ consequently agree on every overlap: the arrow $d_{ij}$ is exactly an isomorphism of the corresponding pairs.

By the sheaf hypothesis on $P_y$, the matching family in step 3 glues to a class in $P_y(T)$. Choose a representative $(x,e)$ with $x\in\mathcal F(T)$ and $e:y\xrightarrow{\sim}q(x)$. Equality of its restriction with the class of $(x_i,e_i)$ gives an isomorphism $c_i:x|_{T_i}\xrightarrow{\sim}x_i$ satisfying $q(c_i)e|_{T_i}=e_i$. On $T_{ij}$ compute
$$q(d_{ij}c_j)e=q(d_{ij})e_j=e_i=q(c_i)e.$$
Cancel the invertible arrow $e$ and use faithfulness of $q_{T_{ij}}$ to obtain $d_{ij}c_j=c_i$. Hence these $c_i$ identify the original descent datum with the pullback of $x$, so it is effective. Along with step 2 this is precisely the etale stack condition of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Only the given sheaf and stack hypotheses, equality of isomorphism classes, and this displayed arrow calculation have been used; no representability is needed.

The site is specialised to etale coverings of S-schemes. Step 1: the Isom sheaf of G plus faithfulness gives separatedness. Step 3: with d_ij:x_j->x_i, effective descent in G gives y and e_i with q(d_ij)e_j=e_i, so the classes match on overlaps. Step 4: I re-derived q(d_ij c_j)e=e_i=q(c_i)e; cancelling e and using faithfulness gives d_ij c_j=c_i, so the datum is effective. The source proof cites no further lemma, so the elementary flags are justified (C1/D3).
